critical_code_review_comments: Route ambiguity: (customer), (admin), and (delivery) all define /order/[id]. Direct URL navigation while logged in as one role can fall through to another group's route (observed 'Insufficient permissions' red-screen when a delivery partner opened /order/<id> via URL). In-app taps route correctly, but hard-links may misroute. Consider distinct paths per role (e.g., /delivery/order/[id], /admin/order/[id]) or a top-level (guarded) /order/[id] that dispatches by role.
server.py: dependency-injection callable naming — require_roles returns 'dep' but the same 'admin' user is being returned; fine functionally but consider renaming for clarity.
server.py list_orders uses alias='status' for the filter param, but customer role never filters by delivery_partner — good; ensure admin listing UI paginates for large datasets (currently limit 500).

rca_of_issue: No blocking issues. Only minor: (a) missing testIDs on address inputs — trivial to add. (b) Expo Router route collision across (admin)/(customer)/(delivery) all owning '/order/[id]' — direct URL nav to /order/<id> as a delivery partner triggered a customer/admin fetch producing 403 red-screen; in-app taps still work because the router keeps the current group context. Fix by disambiguating paths per role group or centralising order detail with role-based branching.
